quotes.name: Manfred Owens
quotes.quote: The book at Oakland Casino Town is mostly the same faces every night, and I'm the one who keeps track of who's in and who's out. Philly runs the floor, Gregory handles the stuff nobody talks about, and I sit near the back with the ledger. The regulars are the ones who've been coming for years — dealers, pit bosses, a few old-timers who just want a seat and a coffee. My shift starts when the evening crowd picks up and ends when the last table closes. It's steady work, but the rhythm is quieter than people think. Most nights it's just the hum of the machines and the clink of chips, and me making sure the numbers line up before I hand the sheet to Philly.

quotes.name: Iris Pham
quotes.quote: I work at a coffee shop, so I know what it's like to be the person behind the counter that nobody thinks to name. When I see the roster for a place like Oakland Casino Town, it's all managers and the big names. But there's a whole crew in the back—cooks, cleaners, security—who show up every shift and keep the place running. They're the ones I see in the neighborhood, grabbing a quick coffee before their shift or heading home after a long night. The roster doesn't carry them because they're not the ones making the decisions or taking the credit. But without them, the whole thing falls apart.
